text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. Most APIs communicate over HTTP requests, where your application sends a request to a server and receives data in return. This data is usually formatted as JSON, a lightweight and easy-to-read structure. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key or token, to prove your identity. Keep in mind that APIs have rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, always include error handling in your code to manage failed requests gracefully and avoid crashes.
